newsitem.title: INDIA: India Kopran to buy stake in Uganda firm.
newsitem.headline: India Kopran to buy stake in Uganda firm.

text.p: Indian pharmaceutical firm Kopran Ltd said it is acquiring Kampala Pharmaceutical Industries (KPI) in Uganda jointly with Industrial Promotion Services, a subsidiary of the Aga Khan Fund for Economic Development (AKFED), at a cost of $5.0 million.
KPI makes capsules, liquids, tablets, oral rehydration products, creams and ointments and achieved a turnover of $5.3 million in 1995, Kopran said in a statement on Tuesday.
The eastern African market has demand for both generic and branded products and Kopran has been exporting various generic products, especially antibiotics, in this region, it said.

"Kopran will licence various brands which is marketed in India. This will enable KPI to sell its products not only in Uganda but also in Kenya, Tanzania, Zaire, Zambia, Malawi and Mozambique," Kopran said.
It said KPI's turnover is expected to touch $10 million by the year 2000.

The Uganda pharmaceutical market is estimated at $30 million out of which half is government business. "KPI being a local company will get price preference while quoting for tenders for government supplies," it said.
